title: Jumbo Jets Find New Life as Hotel Suites
paragraphs: Most Boeing 747s were built to carry hundreds of passengers through the sky.
But two jumbo jets in Malaysia are now offering a very different experience — a place to spend the night.
At 1975 Avenue & Hotel in southern Malaysia, two Boeing 747s have been transformed into hotel suites.
The planes, named Bove and Bey, have a total of 18 suites, which opened to guests in August.
Each suite has design influences from a different country, including Indonesia, Japan, Mexico, Thailand, China, the Czech Republic, Germany, Italy and Switzerland.

With room for up to three people, each suite is split across two floors, giving guests much more space than they'd usually have on a plane — and much less turbulence! The suites also have a king-size bed, a separate living area, and a bathroom with a separate shower and freestanding bath.

The main hotel building stands between the two big planes, offering 20 regular suites for those less interested in staying in a Boeing. The hotel also has a gym and steam room, as well as a jacuzzi, several swimming pools and a water park for children — where kids can play under the tail of one of the planes!

But whether they stay on the jets or in the main hotel, guests won't have to worry about bad plane food. The hotel serves Japanese and German dishes in two different restaurants, while there's also a poolside bar.

The 747 suites may not be flying anywhere, but staying on board can still cost as much as a plane ticket. In September, a night in one of the Boeing 747 suites costs between $420 and $690, depending on the type of suite.
